name: Setting Realistic Contingencies for Los Angeles Commercial Construction Budgets

mainEntity.name: What are realistic contingency percentages for commercial construction budgets in Los Angeles County, and how should owners allocate them?
mainEntity.text: What are realistic contingency percentages for commercial construction budgets in Los Angeles County, and how should owners allocate them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Budget contingency is often under-planned in Los Angeles County commercial projects because owners rely on generic percentages that do not reflect local risk. A more practical approach is to divide contingency into three categories: design, construction, and owner contingency. Design contingency covers inevitable changes as drawings evolve from concept to construction documents. It should be higher when pricing is based on early plans or when the project involves unusual systems, complex façades, or uncertain tenant layouts. Construction contingency addresses field conflicts, unforeseen existing conditions, utility conflicts, and permit-driven changes. It is especially important on renovations and additions, where unknowns in existing buildings are common. Owner contingency covers program changes, finish upgrades, or scope additions initiated by the owner. In fast-changing markets or for first-time commercial developers, this allowance can prevent financial stress when choices shift. In Los Angeles County’s environment of strict codes, multi-agency review, and frequent utility or off-site improvement surprises, using separate contingency buckets and adjusting percentages based on project type, schedule pressure, and drawing maturity is more realistic than applying a single flat number. Owners should periodically revisit contingencies as design and permitting progress, releasing or reallocating funds as key risks are resolved.
acceptedAnswer.description: Commercial construction in Los Angeles County typically warrants higher contingencies than simple industry rules of thumb. Owners should separate design contingency, construction contingency, and owner contingency, adjusting percentages based on project complexity, entitlement risk, and how complete the drawings are at the time of pricing.
